reviews.title: Coming up from the rear?! It's INTEL!
reviews.comment: Edited: 4.5/5. Given how much Intel has drastically improved the performance of this card with new drivers and the continued support, staying on top of their drivers coming out to past and present issues. Additionally, vastly improved performance on DX11 and DX9 titles. This is easily the best affordable entry into PC gaming anyone could buy. If you have the patience to deal with it and technical know how to mess with the feature set of the all-in-one program Intel has provided, this is a no brainer. Especially at an MSRP of $250. A great deal at a fantastic price. Just be aware there are still gonna be some hitches here and there and you have to have patience. So if you're a builder or making a recommendation for a client/friend keep in mind the technical side will rest on you to solve. If that sounds like a headache, go with NVIDIA or AMD (not the 6000 series, AMD while not cancelling support - they sure did show their hand when they attempted to do just that). Original: 3.8/5. Overall Intel has come a long way. Graphically this is a very decent entry level card, but only if you can get it for $250 or less. Why not more? Because the value just isn’t there. Regardless of the strides they’ve made with the drivers this isn’t good for anything using Direct X 11 and not being able to play older titles is a major drawback to this card. Which is a shame because like I said Intel has come far in a short amount of time. XeSS is actually more useful in most games than FSR ever was before 3.1. Even to the point of make the cards performance actually rival an RTX 4060 Ti at times. So if you’re looking at this and think you can make use of this card just make sure you aren’t interested in older software. Also make sure you have a newer CPU to push this GPU because the tests Hardware Unboxed conducted were spot on. This GPU does not like old or low level CPUs. Sadly, I couldn’t use this card in the end, but I genuinely want Intel to keep making GPUs because the PC community need something to cause a ruckus in the GPU landscape. It’d be nice to see NVIDIA and AMD to be competitive again.

reviews.title: Excellent gaming card, can't beat it for the price.
reviews.comment: This is the underdog of gaming cards; the latest versions are a steal for the price.  Nothing comes close.  You should be able to play all your games with zero issues.  In my opinion, gaming in 4k is a waste of money.  Save your money and buy games instead.
reviews.author: Paulgeek

reviews.title: If you get it cheap enough, it’s a solid GPU. Software needs work.
reviews.comment: So far this GPU (managed to get it for roughly $300) functions fairly well. So far I’ve only tested 1080P, but it can run Cyberpunk 2077. With Ray tracing I did have more than a few crashes so it’s not the best GPU in the world but it’s not supposed to be. If you can get one for under $300 (should be $250 MSRP) I’d say it’s worth it. The card itself is very clean looking, not super loud, performance is solid. I did have an issue out of the box. Drivers and Intel software. I couldn’t get a display out for the life of me. Ended up having to swap to an APU (8500G) download the drivers and finally get it working. That could’ve been more of a motherboard issue but it never occurred with other GPU’s I’ve used. (I couldn’t even get a boot menu to display) Outside of that, if you want to stress test this GPU, intel’s monitoring software isn’t great. I’ve yet to find a way to get an overlay for in game performance. Both AMD, and Nvidia have this, Intel needs to catch up in that regard. The software is Intel Graphics Control (formerly ARC control) bit of a downgrade imo. Packaging was super nice, very clean, dare I say classy? Along with the card itself, it has a very clean slim design. If I had gotten this for MSRP, I’d say it’s a great deal, so 4 stars due to having to shell out extra.
